summary.headline: DCW Q4 FY26 PAT rose 60% YoY to Rs.18 crore and FY26 EBITDA rose 11% to Rs.240 crore, with net debt cut to Rs.71 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 revenue was Rs.609 crore (+13.2% YoY, +17% QoQ) and Q4 EBITDA including other income was Rs.70 crore (+14% YoY, +40% QoQ). FY26 revenue was Rs.2,144 crore (+7.2%) and EBITDA Rs.240 crore (+11.2%), with PAT up 60% to Rs.48 crore, helped by lower finance cost. Management said profit growth came from volumes, utilisation and cost gains rather than price, since realisations fell across most products, with C-PVC down more than 20%. Specialty EBITDA fell 6.5% to Rs.177 crore on C-PVC–PVC spread compression, while basic chemicals EBITDA rose to Rs.54 crore from Rs.19 crore. Management withheld FY27 EBITDA guidance and cited pricing volatility from the West Asia conflict; the earlier Rs.400 crore target looks derailed.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (C-PVC, SIOP)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA Rs.177 crore (-6.5%) and margin about 30%, down about 6 points, as C-PVC realisations fell over 20% against unchanged PVC input prices. Q4 EBITDA Rs.39 crore, down 16% YoY and 22% QoQ. SIOP margin is still 35-40%, per management.

segments.name: Basic chemicals (caustic soda, soda ash, chlorine-neutral)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA Rs.54 crore vs Rs.19 crore, with margin 3.5% vs 1.3%, helped by fixed-cost absorption and solar power substitution. Q4 EBITDA Rs.30 crore vs Rs.14 crore a year earlier. Caustic realisation was about $350/t in Q4 and above $400/t in Q1 FY27 per management.

segments.name: Synthetic rutile
segments.commentary: Record FY26 sales volume and reduced inventory. Management guided that the spread should stay elevated vs last year on a better mix from ex-China long-term contracts. It is reported within basic chemicals, and no quarterly realisation was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 EBITDA guidance. CFO said the Rs.400 crore target communicated earlier is 'derailed' by pricing pressure in commodities and specialty; a Rs.300 crore figure could not be confirmed.
Scheduled term loan repayment of about Rs.130 crore in FY27; with Rs.71 crore net debt, the company expects to be net cash positive by end-FY27.
Finance cost for FY27 is guided to fall by about Rs.12-13 crore to around Rs.50 crore, or slightly below, if working-capital credit lines are not used heavily.
The 10 kt final C-PVC phase was completed in late March 2026; benefits are expected from Q1 FY27 and are expected to be annualised over the year.
Management expects caustic and soda ash prices to stay elevated for a couple of quarters; VCM/PVC spreads may be under pressure due to the West Asia conflict.
capex_capacity: C-PVC capacity was raised from 20 kt to 50 kt: 30 kt was added this year, with the final 10 kt completed in late March 2026. C-PVC volumes rose to about 37-38 kt from about 22 kt.
SIOP debottlenecked from 18 kt to 28 kt; output reached 24 kt last year and is now near capacity. Future SIOP spend is aimed at value-added grades, not volume.
Commodity capex will focus on efficiency, not volume. Growth capex will go into specialty or niche chemistries. New capex announcements are on hold until the geopolitical situation clears.
Renewable (solar) project was commissioned in FY26 and substitutes about 25% of power from TNEB. Further solar investment is on hold pending clarity on Tamil Nadu banking rules.
Management said incremental C-PVC payback is about 2-2.5 years at current prices; ROC is 8.56% (slide 20), and management said it would be above 14-15% at 2023-24 commodity prices.
demand_pricing: C-PVC realisations fell more than 20% in FY26 with unchanged PVC input prices, compressing the PVC–C-PVC spread. Management said spreads have returned to pre-war levels, and a pass-through lag in March is expected to normalise in the coming quarter.

Caustic soda operating rates fell in Southeast Asia due to petrochemical feedstock shortages, tightening supply. Demand from paper and textile dipped, but alumina demand is strong, and there has been no production curtailment.
Soda ash import price is about $250/t, and prices are supported by the loss of Iran and Russia imports and higher freight.
Synthetic rutile realisation depends on the export mix; ex-China customers pay better prices. Management is building long-term ex-China contracts.

Management said Epigral, Lubrizol and other new C-PVC capacity still leaves room for imports, so it does not expect a domestic glut. It also noted that dumping cases on PVC and soda ash were not implemented, and that China and Korea C-PVC duties were applied earlier.

PVC feedstock VCM is sourced largely from the Middle East. Supply was disrupted by the Gulf war, so the company is buying at higher cost, which it cannot fully pass through. Management said two European PVC plants (about 2 lakh t, including Vinnolit) closed in 2025, before the conflict.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the caustic soda price firming: cost push or end-user demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to supply disruption: Southeast Asian petrochemical feedstock shortages cut caustic operating rates. It expects this to last until the situation normalises. Q4 realisation was about $350/t and Q1 is above $400/t.

qa_highlights.question: Will the power cost savings from solar be Rs.40-50 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the original target was about Rs.40 crore and later guidance was Rs.25-30 crore. Adjusting for coal prices and volume, savings are about Rs.23-24 crore, and power cost is about Rs.7-8 crore lower in absolute terms.

qa_highlights.question: What finance cost should be expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost should fall by Rs.12-13 crore to about Rs.50 crore, or slightly less, as the company keeps about Rs.200 crore in FDs. Negative carry from working-capital lines could push it up if the war continues.

qa_highlights.question: Are we on track for Rs.2,500 crore revenue, Rs.400 crore EBITDA and net debt-free status by FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt-free by FY27 is on track given Rs.130 crore of repayments, and the company should be net cash positive. The Rs.400 crore EBITDA target is derailed by price erosion, and no EBITDA guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROC and steps to improve it?
qa_highlights.answer: ROC is 8.56%. Management said it will rise with commodity prices and that new investment will focus on high-margin, low-capex projects. It said ROC would be 14-15% or more at 2023-24 commodity prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a glut risk in C-PVC from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic demand still exceeds combined capacity of DCW, Epigral, and Lubrizol, so it sees no mismatch. Imports would fill any gap.

risks_watch: FY27 EBITDA: no guidance given; the Rs.400 crore target is described as derailed, and a Rs.300 crore figure was not confirmed. Track whether C-PVC volume gains (50 kt capacity) offset price erosion.

PVC/VCM spread: VCM is sourced largely from the Middle East and contracts were paused; the company cannot fully pass through higher feedstock cost, and a pass-through lag is expected to normalise in the coming quarter.
Caustic and soda ash: management expects elevated prices for a couple of quarters but declined to forecast beyond that; soda ash anti-dumping duty outcome is pending.
Finance cost and working capital: FY27 finance cost guided to about Rs.50 crore only if working-capital credit lines are not used heavily; negative carry on about Rs.200 crore of FDs persists.
Capex and solar: new capex announcements are on hold pending geopolitical clarity; further solar substitution depends on Tamil Nadu banking rule clarification from TANGEDCO.
C-PVC supply: Epigral and Lubrizol capacity additions; management sees no domestic glut but the 10 kt final phase ramp and import competition need monitoring.
ROC of 8.56% is low; management says it would be 14-15% or more at 2023-24 commodity prices, so returns depend on commodity recovery.
key_quotes: The only thing is that we are definitely not seeing the benefits of the increased CPVC commercialization volumes, because a large part of it is eaten up by the price erosions which we did not anticipate when we gave you a Rs. 400 crores of guidance.
We would not be able to give you a guidance on that , because the prices movement has an impact.
So, in the commodity side it will be more CAPEXES for efficiencies, not for volume.
The spreads have improved. It has gone back to the pre -war.
summary.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet deleveraging, capacity commissioning and volume records, but cautious and evasive on forward numbers. Management declined to give FY27 EBITDA guidance or a Rs.300 crore figure, said Chinese PVC and West Asia developments are too uncertain to forecast, and repeatedly deferred new capex announcements until the geopolitical situation clears.
